title: The Pythagorean Theorem and Its Converse
standard_text: 8.6C use models and diagrams to explain the Pythagorean theorem; 8.7C use the Pythagorean Theorem and its converse to solve problems
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 Pythagorean theorem worksheets for Texas TEKS 8.6C and 8.7C: find the hypotenuse, a missing leg, the converse and real-world problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: a² + b² = c², where c is the hypotenuse.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • In a right triangle, a² + b² = c², where c is the hypotenuse (the side across from the right angle).
  • Find the hypotenuse: add the squares of the legs, then take the square root.
  • Find a leg: subtract, then take the square root: b = √(c² − a²).
  • Converse: if a² + b² = c², the triangle is a right triangle.

Examples

Example

Legs 6 and 8

36 + 64 = 100

√100

Answer: 10

Example

Ladder 10 ft, foot 6 ft from the wall

100 − 36 = 64

√64

Answer: 8 ft

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding the legs: 6 + 8 = 14Square first: 36 + 64 = 100, then √100 = 10.
Forgetting the square rootc² = 100 means c = 10.
Using a leg as the hypotenuseThe hypotenuse is always the longest side.

items.q: In a right triangle, which side is the hypotenuse?
c: The longest side, across from the right angle
items.e: The hypotenuse is the longest side, across from the right angle.

Yes, it is a right triangle

items.q: A 10-foot ladder leans on a wall. Its foot is 6 feet from the wall. How high up the wall does it reach?

Which equation is the Pythagorean theorem for legs a and b and hypotenuse c?
items.e: The squares of the legs add up to the square of the hypotenuse: a² + b² = c².

items.q: Does the Pythagorean theorem work for every triangle?
c: Only for triangles with equal sides
items.e: It only works when one angle is 90°: no, only right triangles.

items.q: A right triangle has legs 6 and 8. Ana says the hypotenuse is 14. What did she do?
items.e: 6 + 8 = 14, but c = √(36 + 64) = 10. She added the legs.

items.q: A right triangle has legs 6 and 8. Ben says the hypotenuse is 100. What did he forget?
items.e: c² = 100, so c = 10. He forgot to take the square root.

items.q: The hypotenuse is 10 and one leg is 6. Kim does 10² + 6². What should she do?
items.e: To find a leg, subtract: b² = 10² − 6² = 64, so b = 8. Subtract: 10² − 6².

items.q: In a right triangle, can a leg be longer than the hypotenuse?
c: Only if the legs are equal
No, the hypotenuse is always the longest
items.e: c² = a² + b² is bigger than a² or b². No, the hypotenuse is always the longest.

items.q: A box is 3 × 4 × 12 units. How long is the longest diagonal from a bottom corner to the opposite top corner?
items.e: First the floor diagonal: 3² + 4² = 25. Then with the height: 25 + 12² = 169. d = √169 = 13.

items.q: A cube has edges of 1 m. How long is a diagonal of one face, exactly?
items.e: 1² + 1² = 2, so the face diagonal is √2 m.

items.e: First the floor diagonal: 2² + 3² = 13. Then with the height: 13 + 6² = 49. d = √49 = 7.

items.q: A cube has edges of 1 m. How long is the diagonal through the cube, exactly?
items.e: 1² + 1² + 1² = 3, so the space diagonal is √3 m.

items.e: First the floor diagonal: 4² + 4² = 32. Then with the height: 32 + 7² = 81. d = √81 = 9.

items.e: √(24² + 18²) = √900 = 30. Yes, the diagonal is 30 in.
